title: Matrix Theory over the Algebra of Ordered Pairs of Normalized Real Numbers
content: We study similarity of matrices over the algebra of ordered pairs of normalized real numbers (OPNs) using its native shifted matrix cubes. For three fixed OPNs centers, the three independently given similarity classes determine the original class in every dimension if and only if all pairwise center differences are units. Three is the least uniform number of such observations. The substantive recovery step is a real matrix theorem: any three distinct real shifts suffice, whereas any two admit a six-dimensional real counterexample. The proof combines a finite-weight argument on a cubic rotation lattice, polynomial interpolation, and noncritical Jordan blocks; critical output blocks need not be used. The OPNs criterion follows through the two real characters of the coefficient algebra. As a complementary invariant, we show that labelled nullities of shifted powers through order ⌈n/2⌉, at all complex scalar parameters, determine similarity with an optimal uniform cutoff. Classical Smith–Fitting invariants and explicit higher evaluation modules place both descriptions in a self-contained algebraic framework.
